_note: Symptom intake: the set questions GilbertOne asks when a patient says what is wrong, as data, so the answers reach the nurse who comes. Not triage. It sets no priority, names no cause, gives no advice; it is a structured set of notes the patient answers for the nurse, one question per turn, every sentence read from here. packages/gilbertone/src/intake.ts reads it and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds it; no phone renders it yet — see platforms.

changelog.what: The headache group derived from the knowledge base: questionsFrom and drawsOn, ten questions of its own, and the flow fixture answering them. Read by packages/catalog/case.json for what the answers are consistent with.

why: The founder's ask of 28 September 2026: a patient told GilbertOne she had a headache and it could not answer her. GilbertOne does not do diagnosis, but it needs to ask the pertinent questions, so that those questions can be taken to the nurse assigned to the patient — so that when the nurse sees the patient, all of those key questions have already been asked by the bot. Deterministic, predefined questions.
whatItIsNot: GilbertOne will not say what is causing this. A nurse or a doctor decides that.
These questions do not decide how urgent it is or where you should be seen.
Nothing here is advice about what to do for it.
Your answers are notes for your nurse, in your own words.

order.rule: The emergency terms in packages/catalog/gilbert-emergency-terms.json are checked on the opening message and on every answer before the intake reads it; the refusal policies in packages/catalog/assistant.json next; the intake last. A red-flag rule is the ratified triage protocol's job and this file carries none — but every answer passes through the existing emergency matcher, so a sentence that names an emergency, typed as an answer to any question, gets the emergency answer and the intake ends there.
order.why: The intake sits at the end of the chain on purpose. Putting a red-flag list here would make it triage without a protocol, which clinical.json refuses; leaving the emergency matcher in front of every answer means the intake can never lower an emergency by being the thing that was listening.

common.why: Asked first for every group, before the group's own questions, so a nurse reads the same shape of note whatever the complaint. The medicine question asks what was used, never whether anything should be.

questions.ask: Since when?
How bad is it right now?
options: Bad enough to stay in bed

questions.ask: Does anything make it better or worse?
What, if anything, have you already used for it? Give the name on the box, or say nothing.
Are there any long-term conditions, allergies or pregnancy the nurse should know about?

groups.name: Headache
groups.questionsFromWhy: Since 29 September 2026 the headache questions are derived from the knowledge base rather than written: questionsFrom names every entry in packages/catalog/knowledge/conditions.json that lists headache among its symptoms, each question names the entries it draws on in drawsOn, and the build holds both lists to each other — every question drawn from an entry, every entry drawn on. A question the base has no entry for says so in keptBecause instead, for the reviewer. Emergency features (a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade, weakness on one side, confusion, the worst headache ever) are never questions: an answer that names one is answered by the emergency words before the intake reads it, and packages/catalog/case.json findings.emergencyFeatures lists them so the build can refuse a question that offers one. What the answers are consistent with is worked out in case.json, for the nurse, never here and never for the patient.

questions.ask: Where in your head is it?
Is light or noise bothering you?
Have you felt sick or vomited with it?
Has anything changed with your sight?
Have you felt dizzy with it?
Have you had any nosebleeds lately?
Is there fever, chills or a sore throat with it?
Have you been in a malaria area in the last few weeks?
Have you had a knock or a fall onto your head recently?
questions.keptBecause: Kept from version one. The knowledge base has no entry for a head injury, so no condition is named behind it; a nurse looks at a knock in person, and the reviewer is asked whether the base should gain the entry or the question should go.

answer.why: The framing around the questions, in the order the conversation reads it. The opening offers and says what GilbertOne will not do; the closing says where the notes are and where they are not. {reviewedBy} is the registration on file. No digit is typed here.
answer.opening: I can take notes for your nurse about this. I will ask a few set questions, one at a time, and write your answers down for the nurse to read at the visit. I will not say what is causing it — that is for your nurse or doctor to work out with you. Shall we start?

consent.labelsWhy: The two chips the offer shows. Each label's words are in the list beside it, so a pressed chip and a typed word are read by the same rule.
consent.declined: All right. Nothing has been written down. Ask me again whenever you like, or book a nurse and tell them at the visit.
consent.unclear: Just say yes to start the notes, or no to leave it.

answer.typeHint: Type your answer below, in your own words.

stop.sentence: Say stop at any point and the questions end there. Whatever you have answered so far stays below for you to show your nurse.
stop.stopped: Stopped. The notes so far are below, and nothing has been sent anywhere.

answer.closing: Nothing has been sent anywhere. Showing or reading them to your nurse at the visit is how they travel today.
answer.arrangeCare: If you have not booked a nurse yet, Book a nurse is where you arrange one.
answer.unmatchedInside: I did not catch an answer. Type a few words, choose one of the options, or say stop to end here.

review.why: No clinician has read these questions. Until one signs — with a registration in the vetting register's own format — the build refuses any question or option that carries a clinical instruction or a digit, and the unreviewed sentence is read on every intake.
review.unreviewed: No clinician has reviewed these questions yet. They are a written list held inside the app, and your nurse will ask her own.
review.reviewed: These questions were reviewed by {reviewedBy}. Your nurse will still ask her own.

summary.title: Notes for your nurse
summary.why: The card the answers are shown on and read from, so the nurse sees the question beside the answer and never an answer alone. Copying puts the card's lines on the clipboard, which is the person's own; nothing is stored by the app.

chip.why: The group the offer opens with when the intake is chosen from a chip, or a message names no complaint the groups know — the general questions, which ask her to say what is wrong in her own words.

platformsWhy: No phone renders the intake yet. iOS and Android join here when their screens exist, and the boundary check refuses a native file that names the intake before this list says so.

fixtures.why: One list every reader of this file runs against its own matcher. Each message says which group it opens, or null when no group does, or emergency when the emergency terms answer it before the intake is asked. The flow runs one whole group and counts the notes.
